**brain-audit reverter-skip: mirrored checks restricted to tree-keyed set**

**What**: Fixed a fail-open in `reverterSkipLine` (brain/scripts/brain-audit.mjs) where the mirrored-check subtraction used ALL of the reverted offender's failing checks unrestricted, instead of only tree-derived ones.
**Why**: `issueLink` (keyed off commit/PR body) and `memoryPresence` (repo-global, reads .memory/ at HEAD) are never causally mirrored by a revert's tree being the byte-exact inverse of the offense — only `adrPresence` and `diffSize` are genuinely tree-derived. Subtracting issueLink/memoryPresence when the reverted offender coincidentally also failed them let a reverter's own independent issue-ref violation get masked, and made verdicts depend on iteration order when a merge tree-matched two different prior offenders.
**Where**: brain/scripts/brain-audit.mjs (new `TREE_KEYED_CHECKS = new Set(['adrPresence','diffSize'])` const, filter applied at the `mirroredChecks` intersection in `reverterSkipLine`, FIX1 JSDoc rewritten to match). Tests: brain/scripts/brain-audit.test.mjs — new fixtures D2 FORGE-C and D2 FORGE-E (two orderings).
**Learned**: When two offenders M1/M2 both happen to be the byte-exact tree-inverse of the same revert R (e.g. offend → revert → identical re-offend → revert again), M1 and M2 necessarily share the SAME tree-derived failing set (both touch the same path) even if they differ in body-keyed checks like issueLink — so restricting the mirrored set to tree-keyed checks also structurally fixes the multi-match ordering bug, not just the single-match masking bug. Mutation-verified: reverting the `TREE_KEYED_CHECKS` filter reddens exactly the two fixtures that depend on it (FORGE-C, FORGE-E closerHasRef:false) and leaves the ordering-safe variant (closerHasRef:true) green, confirming the fix is load-bearing without over-claiming universal reddening.
